input.description: Search docs and memory for IMASM-on-IMASM concept
input.prompt:
Search for the exact concept "IMASM running on IMASM" (or close variants: "self-hosting", "IMASM on IMASM", "the kernel running its own arithmetic", "arithmetic as a real IMASM program", "tokens performing arithmetic") across:
1. ~/imsgct/.claude/projects/-home-mrnob0dy666-imsgct/memory/*.md (the memory files)
2. ~/imsgct/ig-docs/ (search recursively, use command grep -ril since bare grep would skip gitignored files)
3. Any earlier session transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/-home-mrnob0dy666-imsgct/*.jsonl that mention "IMASM running on IMASM" or "IMASM on IMASM" (grep the raw jsonl files for that phrase)

Report back:
- The exact wording of any definition or discussion of this concept you find, with file path and line/context.
- Whether there's already a concrete mechanism in the G-mOMonadOS codebase (under ~/imsgct/G-mOMonadOS/src) for executing real arithmetic (add/multiply/mod/etc.) by running an actual IMASM Program through the kernel's token-based execution loop (self_imscribe, tick, run), as opposed to Rust functions that merely match IMASM's bit encoding. Look at src/kernel.rs, src/tokens.rs, and search for any existing "imasm arithmetic" or "token arithmetic" implementation.
- Keep the report under 400 words. Quote exact source text where you find it rather than paraphrasing, since precision matters here.

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. content.text:
**Task**: searched memory, ig-docs, and session transcripts for "IMASM running on IMASM" / self-hosting / token-arithmetic precedent, and checked whether the kernel already runs real arithmetic as an actual IMASM program.

**Findings:**

1. No prior documented definition of "IMASM running on IMASM" exists anywhere. `command grep` across `~/.claude/projects/-home-mrnob0dy666-imsgct/memory/*.md` (all ~140 files) and `~/imsgct/ig-docs/` for that phrase, "self-hosting," "tokens performing arithmetic," "arithmetic as a real IMASM program," and "kernel running its own arithmetic" returns nothing. The one jsonl hit is the current session's own transcript recording this very search request — self-referential, not prior precedent. This phrase is Lando's own fresh directive, not a term this repo has used before.

2. No existing mechanism runs arithmetic by executing a real IMASM `Program` through the kernel's token loop. Checked `src/kernel.rs`: `tick()` (line 280), `run()` (487), `self_imscribe()` (669) are the real execution primitives, but they interpret the twelve-token instruction set, not arithmetic. `src/tokens.rs` has no `enum Token` findable by that exact name via grep (the type may be defined via macro or under different casing — not confirmed).

3. Structural fact worth surfacing directly: from prior session context, IMASM's full opcode set is exactly twelve tokens — Vinit, Tanch, Afwd, Arev, Clink, Evalt, Fsplit, Ffuse, Imscrib, Evalf, Engagr, Ifix — one per canonical mark (⊢⊣≻≺⋈⊤∈∋⊙⊥⊞⊡). These are categorical/structural operations (initialize, terminate, forward/reverse morphism, split, fuse, evaluate-true/false, engage, fix), not arithmetic opcodes. There is no add/subtract/multiply/divide/modulo token in the instruction set as currently defined anywhere I found.

Implication for the parent thread, stated as a fact not a recommendation: "IMASM running on IMASM" for arithmetic cannot mean finding an existing add/multiply mechanism, since none exists. It would mean either composing arithmetic out of sequences of the twelve structural tokens (an unbuilt construction) or locating a bridge outside `G-mOMonadOS/src` — my search was scoped to that directory's `kernel.rs`/`tokens.rs` only, so a bridge elsewhere in the repo tree is not ruled out.
